 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Zach Edey accounted for 23 points (10-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 10 rebounds, one assist and two blocks in Monday’s win over the Wizards. 
 Back in the Grizzlies’ lineup after missing the last two games, Edey had an excellent night in the nation’s capital. Shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line, the 7-foot-4 center finished with a season-high point total and his second double-double of the season. It’s just one game, but Edey’s performance against the Wizards may have closed his “buy low” window. 
 Cam Spencer 
 MEM 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Edey is back after a two-game absence and will start, returning to his usual starting center role. However, the Grizzlies remain without Ty Jerome (hip), so Spencer starts again at point guard and is worth streaming. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart (illness) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Wizards. 
 Stewart has started two straight in place of Zach Edey (ankle), but the former will sit this one out, while Edey gets a questionable tag. Even if Edey returns, the absence of Stewart should allow Taylor Hendricks to log some additional playing time. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart (illness) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Stewart has started the Grizzlies’ last two games at center, filling in for the injured Zach Edey (ankle). Both are questionable for Monday, as is Quentin Post (concussion). If they all sit, the Grizzlies will likely have to go small, with Taylor Hendricks, Olivier-Maxence Prosper and Kris Murray playing more minutes. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Zach Edey (ankle) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Edey has missed the Grizzlies’ last two games, with Isaiah Stewart replacing him in the starting lineup. Beef Stew, who is also questionable due to an illness, should get another start if Edey can’t play on Monday, provided he’s available. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Zach Edey (ankle) has been ruled out against the Nets on Saturday. 
 Edey will miss a second straight game, which should allow Isaiah Stewart to remain in the starting lineup for another. He contributed 12 points, five rebounds and four blocks in Friday’s blowout win over the Pelicans. 
 Zach Edey 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #14 
 Zach Edey (ankle) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Nets. 
 Edey missed Friday’s game against the Pelicans with an ankle injury and is questionable for Saturday’s matchup with the Nets. If he’s ruled out again, Isaiah Stewart could start again. 
 Isaiah Stewart 
 MEM 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Isaiah Stewart put up 12 points (5-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, and four blocks in start against the Pelicans. 
 In his start, he was physical and took advantage of the Pelicans defense. He won’t ever be a high-level fantasy player, but he gets the job done. Zach Edey doesn’t play back to backs at this point, so if the Grizzlies decide to rest him, Stewart can be worth a stream. 
 Cameron Boozer 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 #27 
 The Memphis Grizzlies will start Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer, and Isaiah Stewart on Friday against the Pelicans. 
 Zach Edey is out due to injury management, so Isaiah Stewart will get the start against the Pelicans. Stewart could be used as a stream in redraft leagues, especially since Quinten Post is already out, so Stewart is projected to get plenty of minutes. 
 Quinten Post 
 MEM 
 Center 
 #41 
 Quinten Post (concussion) has been ruled out against the Pelicans on Friday. 
 Post will miss a second straight game due to this concussion. With Zach Edey (ankle) out, Isaiah Stewart should start at center, with Cameron Boozer filling out some minutes as the backup center.

 Klay Thompson recorded 17 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two assists, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Rockets.
 Thompson has made at least five three-pointers in three of his last four appearances, providing the spacing the Heat hoped for when they signed him.  Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 20 points (8-of-11 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, one steal and three blocks in Monday’s win over the Rockets.
 While Antetokounmpo failed to score in the first quarter of Monday’s game, he did a bit of everything else. The Heat forward recorded eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and two blocks in the frame. Giannis scored six points in the second quarter and 14 in the third, extending his run of at least 20 points to 11 straight games. If Bam Adebayo (hip) misses time, Giannis will be even more important to the Heat than he already is.
